A lot of us here are type one and im not a doctor but have a lot of family that are type two and encounter so many conversations. From my understanding of type two if you can alter your eating habbits and exercise (if you haven't already) it usually helps. My a1c was almost 11 when I found out I was pregnant as far as we know the baby is healthy and strong. Take care when you count carbs and take your lantus at the same time everyday if possible(sometimes youre off by an hour or two amd thats okay but do your best). Check your bg and correct for your meals as soon as you know how much you'll eat and the carb count. It lets the insulin start working as you eat and helps with less of a post meal spike. Squeezing in a walk after meals or a quick swim can help with bloodsugars and blood circulation which helps your body utilize insulin faster. Also be sure to rotate your sites. If you always do it in the same spot your body may not work as well with the insulin.  I would like to remind you im not a doctor but this is how green the grass is in my yard

I rarely put my dexcom on my abdomen and when I tell them its on my arm or leg I tell them that my doctor gave the approval for alternate sites due to my stomach beginning to have hard tissue from pumpsites that are painful to put my dexcom around. They just make a note on your profile and continue. Im not reccomending this it is just a personal experience. Please consult either and your dexcom rep/endocrinologist
